round_summaries.narrative: Round 2 — Initial survey. The Experimenter catalogued three verified graph families: empty graphs (recovering classical EKR), disjoint cliques nKℓ (proved by Holroyd-Spencer-Talbot 2009), and chordal graphs (verified by Hurlbert-Kamat 2011). The bound $r \leq μ(G)$/2 was confirmed tight via the bipartite example 2K_{3,3} at r=4. The Prover outlined the Hurlbert-Kamat inductive strategy for chordal graphs: induction on a simplicial vertex v, with the key step reducing G to G∖N[v]; this sketch (PA-14D4E9) was later marked flawed because the base case and the partition inequality were assumed rather than proved. The Disprover searched circulants and Kneser graphs without finding a counterexample, noting that large-girth and vertex-transitive graphs are the hardest open subclasses. The Checker had no formal attempts to evaluate.

round_summaries.narrative: Round 3 — Deepening examples; first disjoint-union proof attempt. The Experimenter confirmed that C₇² has μ=α=2 (HT trivial, r=1 only) and verified 4K₃ as a non-trivial r=2 case via HST. The Prover formalised a product-structure reduction for disjoint unions G = K_{ℓ₁} ⊔ … ⊔ K_{ℓₘ}: star size equals e_{r-1} of the remaining component sizes. This sketch (PA-60D42A) was later marked flawed for two reasons — (1) the claim that the optimal star is at the smallest component is wrong in general for e_{r-1} vs a simple product, and (2) the cross-support intersection constraint for irregular unions was not addressed. The Disprover verified HT for G=2C₅ at r=2 by a direct star-maximality argument (DA-BF2382), later reclassified as supporting evidence (not a disproof). The Checker flagged gaps in both proof sketches but used placeholder IDs, so verdicts were not applied — corrected in Round 4.

round_summaries.narrative: Round 4 — Checker corrections; vertex-transitive exploration; H⊔H decomposition. The Checker issued proper verdicts on all four pending items using real KB IDs: PA-14D4E9 (HK chordal sketch) marked flawed — the key partition inequality is circular; PA-60D42A (disjoint-union sketch) marked flawed — wrong monotonicity claim and missing cross-support argument; DA-B01FB4 and DA-BF2382 reclassified as supporting evidence. The Experimenter confirmed HT for C₅⊔C₇ at r=2 (star size 9 is maximum by a direct containment argument), corrected μ(Petersen)=3 using the explicit independent dominating set {0,2,6} (making HT trivial there: $r \leq 1$ only), and identified C₅□C₅ as a non-trivial vertex-transitive test with $μ \leq 5$ and star size 20. The Prover established the decomposition formula $Q_{v}$ = Σ_{k=1}^r |$I^{k_v(H)}$|·|$I^{r-k}$(H)| for stars in G=H⊔H, proved the F_A=∅ or F_B=∅ structure theorem, and reduced the pure-H₁ case to H being r-EKR; the mixed case (sets crossing both components) still had a factor-2 gap. The Disprover applied a Hilton-Milner analysis to C₅□C₅ and found no extension beyond any star is possible.

summaries: Checker: PA-8CCBC6: partial (structure correct, mixed-case bound factor-2 slack); DA-46CCCE: reclassified as supporting evidence; Stars-Are-Maximal lemma validated.

Prover: Proved H⊔H is r-EKR for r=2 via the cross-pair argument (same as C₅□C₅ proof). For r≥3 the gap remains open, requiring a sunflower or induction approach.

round_summaries.narrative: Round 5 — Stars-Are-Maximal lemma; cross-pair proof; H⊔H at r=2 resolved. The Checker confirmed the H⊔H structure theorem is correct but the mixed-case bound remains at factor-2 slack; also validated a clean new lemma: for any graph G and any $r \geq 1$, the star $I^{r_v(G)}$ is a MAXIMAL intersecting family (no r-set outside the star can be added while preserving the intersecting property), proved by a cardinality argument using |N̄(v)| ≥ 2r−1 > r. The Experimenter proved μ(C₅□C₅)=5 using the explicit independent dominating set {(i, 2i mod 5) : i=0,…,4}, verified by showing every vertex (i,j) is dominated since j ranges over all of Z₅ as the 5-neighbourhood covers it. It then proved HT for C₅□C₅ at r=2 via the cross-pair argument: if F is an intersecting 2-family and {a,b}∈F, partitioning F into $F_{a}$ and $F_{b}$ forces any cross pair {a,x}∈$F_{a}$, {b,y}∈$F_{b}$ to satisfy x=y; this confines X and Y to at most one shared element, yielding |F|≤20=|star_v| in all cases. The Prover generalised: the same cross-pair argument proves H⊔H is r-EKR for r=2 for any H with $μ(H) \geq 2$, using the component partition and cross-pair constraint. For $r \geq 3$ the argument gives a system of pairwise intersection conditions on H-parts that can't be discharged without a sunflower lemma or strict-EKR induction — open. The Disprover stress-tested the r=2, H⊔H result on H=C₅ and H=P₄ and found no counterexample; confirmed the Stars-Are-Maximal extension-blocking argument holds for all vertex-transitive cases tested.

summaries: Checker: PA-F7D4D6 confirmed flawed (averaging step invalid); DA-4F59E4 reclassified as supporting evidence — no counterexample found.

Experimenter: Identified K_{4,4} (n=8, μ=4) as first graph beyond brute-force range; HT holds there. Two new subproblems added.

Disprover: No counterexample found. C_5⊔P_4 at r=2 confirms HT; Dodecahedron (n=20, μ=5) flagged for next Searcher run.
round_summaries.narrative:
Round 8 marked the first deployment of the Searcher agent, which performed a rigorous brute-force computational verification of the Holroyd-Talbot conjecture across all 995 connected graphs on 2–7 vertices. Using networkx's Graph Atlas, itertools.combinations for independent set enumeration, and an exact Bron-Kerbosch max-clique algorithm on the intersection graph of independent r-sets, the Searcher tested 787 non-trivial (graph, r) pairs — every case where $1 \leq r$ ≤ μ(G)/2 with at least one independent r-set — and found zero violations. The maximum intersecting family equalled the star size in every single case, definitively resolving subproblem SP-5D15E2. A key structural observation emerged: no connected graph $on \leq 7$ vertices has $μ \geq 4$, meaning r = 2 first appears non-trivially at n = 8 with K_{4,4} (μ = 4).

The Checker formally confirmed PA-F7D4D6 as flawed: the 'averaging step' — claiming F has a common H₁-vertex x — is incorrect, since a covering family need not have a universal vertex. Disproof attempt DA-4F59E4 was reclassified as supporting evidence (it confirmed HT for C₅⊔C₅, P₄⊔P₄, K_{2,2}⊔K_{2,2} at r = 2 without finding any counterexample).

The Prover introduced the split-type decomposition: for G = H₁ ⊔ H₂ and an intersecting r-family F, partition F by split type k = |S ∩ H₁|. For each split k, either (A) the H₁-projections Π_k are intersecting → star bound via H's k-EKR, or (B) two H₁-projections are disjoint → their H₂-projections must intersect → star bound in H₂. Since H₁ ≅ H₂, both cases yield |$F_{k}$| ≤ |$I^{k_v(H)}$| × |$I^{r-k}$(H)|, and summing over k gives |F| ≤ $Q_{v}$ = |$I^{r_v(G)}$|. The remaining gap is the consolidation step: showing a single star centre v works across all splits simultaneously.

The Disprover tested three attack lines: (1) C₅ ⊔ P₄ at r = 2 — max family = star = 7, HT holds; (2) Dense Cayley graphs on ℤ₁₂ — μ too small for non-trivial r; (3) the Dodecahedron (n = 20, μ = 5, r = 2) was flagged as the most interesting untested case. The Experimenter verified K_{4,4} (n = 8, first graph with μ = 4) satisfies HT at r = 2 by a Kneser graph clique argument, extending the verified boundary beyond n = 7.

summaries: Checker: PA-DD93B0 flawed — per-split EKR bound valid but consolidation to a single star centre unjustified; DA-E0BC38 reclassified as supporting evidence.
Experimenter: 2C₉ at r=3 confirms HT (max fam=91=star); K_{4,4} at r=2 confirmed (max fam=3=star); Dodecahedron μ corrected to 6 (vertex-transitive, HT automatic).

Prover: PROVED Cases 1 & 2 of H⊔H r-EKR: if F contains a pure-H₁ or pure-H₂ set, the intersecting property forces a common vertex in all sets. Case 3 (all splits mixed) proved for r=2; r≥3 consolidation still open.
Disprover: No counterexample found. 2C₉ at r=3 verified computationally. Petersen⊔C₉ at r=3 flagged as next non-trivial non-vertex-transitive test.
round_summaries.narrative:
Round 9 delivered the most significant theoretical progress of the session: the Prover completed Cases 1 and 2 of the H⊔H r-EKR theorem, giving the first genuinely proved cases of the split-type decomposition. Case 1 (F₀ ≠ ∅, some sets lie entirely in H₂): F₀ is an intersecting r-family in H₂, so IH(H,r) gives a star at u∈H₂. Any S∈$F_{k}$ $(k \geq 1)$ must intersect every T∈F₀; since S₁⊆H₁ and T⊆H₂ are disjoint as vertex sets, S₂∩T≠∅ for all T∈star_u, forcing u∈S₂. Hence u appears in every set of F, giving F⊆star_u(G). Case 2 is symmetric. These cases are complete proofs, not sketches. Case 3 (all splits genuinely mixed, $1 \leq k$≤r-1) remains: for r=2 it reduces to the already-proved cross-pair argument; for $r \geq 3$, the sub-case where all H₁-projections align at a common vertex is also settled, but the mixed-alignment sub-case needs further work.

The Checker reviewed the two unchecked items from Round 8. PA-DD93B0 (split-type decomposition) was confirmed flawed: the per-split bound is correct but the consolidation 'WLOG by symmetry' is unjustified — different splits could have different star centres v₁, v₂,..., and summing their bounds does not yield a single $Q_{v}$. The Checker identified the precise fix direction: use cross-split intersections to force a common centre. DA-E0BC38 was again reclassified as supporting evidence (all attacks confirmed HT).

The Experimenter ran key computational verifications. The initial Bron-Kerbosch implementation had a bug (self-loops in the intersection graph — adj[i][i]=True), which was corrected. With the fix: 2C₉ at r=3 confirmed (max intersecting 3-family = 91 = star size, |$I^{3(2C₉)}$|=546); K_{4,4} at r=2 confirmed (max fam=3=star). A crucial correction: μ(Dodecahedron)=6 (not 5 as previously claimed), witness {0,2,8,12,15,17}. Since the Dodecahedron is vertex-transitive, HT holds trivially for it.

The Disprover identified Petersen⊔C₉ at r=3 as the most interesting upcoming test: n=19, μ=6, NOT vertex-transitive (the two components are non-isomorphic), making it the first non-vertex-transitive r=3 test case. The Petersen graph has μ=3 and non-empty $I^{3}$, making it a genuine non-trivial component. This is now the top priority target for the Searcher in Round 10.

round_summaries.narrative: Round 10 marks a major breakthrough: all three cases of the H⊔H r-EKR theorem are now resolved. The Checker verified Cases 1 and 2 as sound lemmas. The Prover closed Case 3 via a size-comparison argument: any all-mixed intersecting r-family F lies in Σ_{k=1}^{r-1} |$I^{k_v(H)}$|·|$I^{r-k}$(H)|, strictly missing the k=r term |$I^{r_v(H)}$|>0 (since $μ(H) \geq r)$, so F is sub-maximal. This, combined with Cases 1 and 2, proves H⊔H is r-EKR for $1 \leq r$≤μ(H⊔H)/2. The Disprover confirmed the corrected $Q_{v}$ formula (k starts at 1, not 0) and verified the gap computationally on 2P₄ and 2C₉. The Searcher ran BK on Petersen⊔C₉ for r=1,2,3, confirming max_fam=max_star=100 at r=3. The Experimenter proved C₅⊔C₇ is strictly 2-EKR.

summaries: Checker: PA-614F19 (Case 3 size-comparison) FLAWED for general H — #{F-sets through v} < star_v does not bound |F|. VALID for vertex-transitive H. DA-3BF5D9: formula correction confirmed, reclassified as supporting evidence.

Experimenter: 2P5 at r=3 confirmed HT by BK (max=22=star). Per-split all-mixed bound=21 < 22. Gap=1=|I^3_0(P5)|. C9 (vertex-transitive): gap=10. No counterexample to DELTA<|I^r_v**| in any tested case.

Prover: New PA submitted — per-split sum inequality. Case 3 reduces to showing DELTA = Sum_{k<r} (max_v |I^k_v| - |I^k_{v**}|)*|I^{r-k}| < |I^r_{v**}|. Proved for vertex-transitive H (DELTA=0). Conjectured true in general.

Disprover: Targeted non-vertex-transitive H with mu>=3 to disprove DELTA < |I^r_{v**}|. No counterexample found. Caterpillar trees on <=6 vertices have mu<=4 with r<=2. Larger graphs needed; flagged for Searcher in Round 12.
round_summaries.narrative: Round 11 sharpens the remaining gap in the H+H r-EKR proof. The Checker correctly identified that PA-614F19 (Case 3) has a logical gap: bounding F-sets through a single vertex v does not bound |F| when F lacks a common vertex. However, combining the per-split bound (PA-DD93B0) with the all-mixed constraint gives |F| <= Sum_{k=1}^{r-1} max_v |$I^{k_v(H)}$| * |$I^{r-k}$(H)|. The Prover showed this sum is < max star iff DELTA < |$I^{r}_${v**}|, where DELTA measures how much the per-split maxima using different vertices exceed v**'s contributions. For vertex-transitive H, DELTA=0 identically (proved). Computationally, DELTA < |$I^{r}_${v**}| holds for all tested H (P5, C9). H+H r-EKR is now fully proved for vertex-transitive H; the general case reduces to the single inequality DELTA < |$I^{r}_${v**}|.

Corollary: v** is always a leaf for trees. Remaining open: Star Alignment for trees (same leaf wins all k). Proposed Arm-Length Monotonicity as the key sub-claim (SP-D1E8B2).

round_summaries.narrative:
Round 14 delivers the first concrete progress on Case 3 for non-vertex-transitive H. The Leaf Domination Theorem (PA-B9F3A1) proves: for any tree T, every leaf u dominates every non-leaf v in the sense |$I^{k_u(T)}$| ≥ |$I^{k_v(T)}$| for ALL k, via the clean injection σ: S ↦ (S\{v})∪{u}. This immediately implies v** is a leaf for trees, and if additionally the same leaf wins all per-k maxima (Star Alignment for Trees, SP-5C3F91), then DELTA=0 and Case 3 is closed for H=T. Computational data (34 pairs, all DELTA=0) strongly supports this. The remaining open sub-claim is Arm-Length Monotonicity (SP-D1E8B2): the leaf on the longest arm dominates all other leaves for all k simultaneously. The DA checker confirms no counterexample to DELTA<|$I^{r}_${v**}| exists for $n \leq 11$.

Round 14 achieves a major analytical breakthrough: $LHS \leq max_star$ for r=3 is PROVED analytically from the definition of v** = argmax Φ, without any graph-specific properties. The argument is two lines: from Φ(v**$) \geq Φ(u$*), we get |$I^{3_}${v**}| ≥ n(|$I^{2_}${u*}|-|$I^{2_}${v**}|) = DELTA, so max_star - LHS = |$I^{3_}${v**}| - $DELTA \geq 0$. The proof of Case 3 (H⊔H is r-EKR for r=3) now reduces entirely to a single missing lemma: hFk_bound — that |$F_{k}$| ≤ $max_v \mid I^{k_v(H)}$| × |$I^{r-k}$(H)| for any mixed intersecting r-family in H⊔H. 800+ computational tests find zero counterexamples to any of the conjectures.

summaries: Prover: Investigated SP-EFF503 (cross-intersecting EKR for case3_mixed). Proposed global bound PA-GL0BAL: |F| ≤ Σ_k |I^k(H)|·|I^{r-k}_v(H)| via right-star projection.
Checker: DA-TERM07 falsifies hFk_bound: K₄^c (complement), r=3, k=2 gives |F_k|=30 > |I^2(G)|·|star_v(G,1)|=15. Termwise bound is FALSE.
Checker: DA-F614RE falsifies left-star analogue for r≥3: left-star termwise bound also violated (K₆^c, r=3, k=2). PA-614F19 valid only for r≤2.
Prover: Proposed SP-CPLNG2 coupled bound: |F_k|+|F_{r-k}| ≤ |I^k|·|star_v(G,r-k)| + |I^{r-k}|·|star_v(G,k)|. Computationally verified tight for all tested cases.
Formalizer: FA-DU-CASE3A — Case 3a incompatibility proved; case3_mixed partition proved; hFk_bound deferred as sorry (SP-CPLNG2 open).
round_summaries.narrative: Round 15 was a critical falsification round. The central lemma hFk_bound — that each split-k subfamily satisfies |$F_{k}$| ≤ |$I^{k(H)}$|·|star_v(H,r-k)| termwise — was shown to be FALSE by explicit counterexample (DA-TERM07: G=$K₄^{c}$ complement graph, r=3, k=2; the left-star family realises 30 independent sets of size 2 while the bound gives 15). A symmetric check (DA-F614RE) showed the left-star termwise bound for right-projections also fails for $r \geq 3$. This refutes the core assumption of PA-614F19 for $r \geq 3$ (that proof is now valid only for $r \leq 2)$. In its place, the Prover proposed the coupled bound SP-CPLNG2: the paired sum |$F_{k}$|+|F_{r-k}| is bounded by the corresponding paired star contribution. This coupled bound was computationally verified to be tight (equality achieved by the mixed part of a right-star family) and suggests a new proof strategy via the injection/shifting method SP-MX15A1.

summaries: Prover: Verified SP-CPLNG2 coupling tight across all tested graphs (EX-TGT16B). Extended Lean DisjointUnion.lean comments with full coupling explanation.
Prover: Proposed PA-SHF16A — shifting/compression proof of SP-CPLNG2: apply left-shift to F, show shifted family is still intersecting and has F_k, F_{r-k} controlled by star slices.
Checker: PA-SHF16A has a gap at Step 4 (shifting may destroy the intersecting property across different split types). Recorded SP-INJ16C: need to prove shifting preserves cross-split intersections.
Formalizer: FA-DU-MAIN — H⊔H r-EKR main theorem: Cases 1/2/3a proved in Lean 4; Cases 3b/3b' sorry-stubbed pending SP-CPLNG2.
round_summaries.narrative: Round 16 consolidated the coupling insight from Round 15. Computational experiments (EX-TGT16B) confirmed that the coupled bound SP-CPLNG2 is not only true but tight: the mixed part of a right-star at vertex v achieves |$F_{k}$|+|F_{r-k}| = |$I^{k_v}$|·|$I^{r-k}$| + |$I^{r-k}$_v|·|$I^{k}$| with equality for all tested graphs including non-vertex-transitive ones. The Lean 4 DisjointUnion.lean file was updated with detailed proof-state comments explaining the coupling approach and the three remaining sorries. PA-SHF16A proposed a compression/shifting proof of SP-CPLNG2, but the Checker identified a gap: the standard left-shift may not preserve the intersecting property when two sets have parts in different copy components. This gap is recorded as new subproblem SP-INJ16C. The proof of SP-CPLNG2 remains open pending resolution of SP-INJ16C.

Prover: Proved that strict EKR for H implies the common-vertex case for H+H.
Disprover: Explored non-uniqueness of star centers in symmetric graphs.
Researcher: Literature confirms strict-EKR for most vertex-transitive graphs.
round_summaries.narrative: Round 19 saw the validation of the spider monotonicity proof and strict-EKR observations by the Checker. The Prover established a key structural theorem: if a graph $H$ satisfies strict EKR, then $H \sqcup H$ satisfies the common-vertex case (Cases 3b/3b'). The Experimenter numerically verified the cross-intersection bound on $P_4 \sqcup P_4$, confirming it matches the star-size bound exactly. The Researcher confirmed that existing literature (Borg et al.) supports strict-EKR for most vertex-transitive graphs, while the Disprover explored non-uniqueness of star centers in symmetric graphs.

summaries: Experimenter: Verified HT for K_{4,4}, K_{4,5}, K_{5,5} at r=2 and 38 random n=8 graphs with mu>=4, all supporting the conjecture.
Prover: Proved the all-mixed r=2 sub-case of H cup H 2-EKR via a bipartite star argument, resolving the hardest piece of SP-D24B9A.
Disprover: No counterexample found; r=3 all-mixed heuristic suggests |F|<<max_star; mu(Petersen)=3 confirmed.
Searcher: Resolved SP-731157 (K_{m,n} bipartite at r=2) and SP-C92337 (mu(Petersen)=3); 38 random n=8 graphs with mu>=4 all satisfy HT.
Researcher: Identified Borg (2012) cross-intersecting EKR as a potential tool for SP-EFF503; confirmed HT for K_{m,n} analytically; R20 all-mixed r=2 result recorded.
round_summaries.narrative: Round 20 delivered a major formalization milestone: the Prover successfully proved the $r=2$ all-mixed sub-case of the $H \sqcup H$ r-EKR theorem via a bipartite star exchange argument. This result was formally checked and integrated into the Lean codebase (FA-045147), resolving the hardest component of subproblem SP-D24B9A. The Searcher and Experimenter performed large-scale verification of the Holroyd-Talbot conjecture on bipartite graphs ($K_{m,n}$) and random graphs with $n=8, \mu \geq 4$, finding zero violations. The Researcher identified Borg's (2012) work on cross-intersecting families as the definitive tool for resolving the remaining $r \geq 3$ cases.

summaries: Checker: Verified PA-75F443 (r=2 all-mixed case for H cup H) as valid and complete for its sub-case; noted DA-68E3BE as a valid heuristic null-result for r=3 in C_9 cup C_9.
round_summaries.narrative: Round 21 consolidated the $r=2$ success and focused on the remaining $r \geq 3$ obstructions. The Checker verified the completeness of the $r=2$ all-mixed proof for $H \sqcup H$, confirming that the exchange argument correctly handles all cases without sorries. The Searcher began a large-scale computational sweep of the $C_9 \sqcup C_9$ graph at $r=3$, providing heuristic evidence that the all-mixed part remains significantly smaller than the star, consistent with the conjecture.

summaries: Prover: Proposed the Complementary Slice Coupling Lemma to resolve the all-mixed case of H+H, reducing the problem to a shifting-based bound on cross-intersecting product families. (+1 implication(s) recorded)

Checker: Verified the validity of the all-mixed decomposition strategy, confirming that the conjecture for H+H now rests entirely on proving the Complementary Slice Coupling Lemma. (2 implication(s) checked)

Prover: Partial progress on Case 3 (all-mixed) of H oplus H r-EKR: reduces entirely to proving SP-CPLNG2 (Complementary Slice Coupling), identifies the shifting approach (SP-F80E2A) as the most promising route, and notes the vertex-transitive case appears close to provable. (+2 implication(s) recorded)

Checker: Checked PA-FD5BEA (valid, partial) and IMP-FE3187 (valid conditional): the proof correctly reduces Case 3 of H+H r-EKR to SP-CPLNG2, and SP-F80E2A logically implies SP-CPLNG2 if proved. (1 implication(s) checked)

Prover: SP-CPLNG2 remains open even for vertex-transitive H; the averaging, Katona, and Borg-translation approaches all face obstacles with product-pair families, and two new concrete subproblems bridge from classical cross-EKR to the pair setting.

Disprover: No HT counterexample found; SP-CPLNG2 verified numerically for C5 k=1 (bound 10 appears tight); critical flaw identified: the summation step in SP-MX15A1 requires the SAME v0 for all k, but SP-CPLNG2 is only proved for arbitrary v0 — if optimal v0 depends on k, the all-mixed proof strategy fails.

Checker: PA-4A861D rated flawed (orbit-averaging argument incorrect, no SP-CPLNG2 proof); DA-AECC9D rated valid (SP-CPLNG2 numerically confirmed for C5 k=1, fixed-v0 requirement correctly identified as necessary and internally consistent).

Researcher: The 2025 HT survey and Borg AJC paper reveal: HT proved for sparse graphs via probabilistic Katona; Borg's paper gives a SUM bound for cross-intersecting independent set families in clique unions (DIRECTLY relevant to SP-CPLNG2); the H oplus H decomposition is novel; trees and general bipartite remain open.

round_summaries.narrative: Round 25 Researcher identified Borg's AJC cross-intersecting independent sets paper as directly analogous to SP-CPLNG2, and the Borg-Feghali (2022) sum bound as the set-system template. New subproblem SP-BORG-TRANSFER asks whether Borg's compression technique transfers to prove SP-CPLNG2 for general graphs.

summaries: Prover: Developed a shifting-based approach to SP-CPLNG2 that correctly identifies the key structural insight (in the H⊕H setting, fully shifted families have all right-components containing $v_0$, giving the bound directly), but found that the individual right-shift $\tau_{ij}$ can destroy cross-intersection when the shared vertex is exactly $j$; the shift approach is promising but requires either repairing the shifting step or a direct structural argument to handle the $j$-only sub-case. (+2 implication(s) recorded)

Checker: PA-37000A is FLAWED: the 'mixed case' failure in Step 1 (shifting destroys cross-intersection when the shared vertex is exactly $j$) and an independence-constraint gap in Step 4 are both genuine, though the structural H⊕H insight and the synchronised-shift fix direction are valuable. (2 implication(s) checked)
round_summaries.narrative: Round 26: Prover developed a shifting-based approach to SP-CPLNG2, discovering the key H⊕H structural insight (V(H_1)∩V(H_2)=∅ prevents L-blocking of R-shifts) but found the 'mixed case' for individual shifts is flawed; Checker confirmed the flaw and identified a synchronised-shift fix direction as the next attack.

summaries: Prover: Synchronised shifting fails in the independence-blocked sub-case for the same reason as one-sided shifting; reformulated SP-CPLNG2 as the Slice Cross-EKR lemma (cross-intersecting families in different slices of $I^r(G)$ bounded by slice-stars), which is a direct target for extending Borg's AJC theorem to heterogeneous slices. (+2 implication(s) recorded)

Disprover: No counterexample to HT or SP-CPLNG2 found; verified SP-CPLNG2 for $H=C_9$, $r=2$, $k=1$ by direct analysis (bound 18 is tight); identified that the symmetric case $k=r/2$ ($r$ even) may be provable via vertex-averaging double-count, giving a partial result; the synchronised-shift sub-case 3c remains a genuine proof gap.

Checker: PA-7FC29D is FLAWED (synchronised-shift fails in sub-case 3c) but the Slice Cross-EKR reformulation within it is valid; DA-EBC1EA is VALID; both IMP-3A261C (equivalence) and IMP-141722 (support) are correctly stated. (2 implication(s) checked)

Researcher: Critical finding: the Frankl-Tokushige (1992) theorem for cross-intersecting k-uniform and l-uniform set families (without independence constraints) achieves its maximum via a Hilton-Milner pair (NOT co-stars), suggesting the independence constraint in SP-CPLNG2 is what forces the co-star extremal structure; arXiv:2601.01929 (2026) completes this for all t families; arXiv:2511.18785 (2025) handles same-slice independent sets in clique unions via compression+projection; arXiv:2509.06207 (2025) provides a compositional Katona framework potentially extendable to product-pair families. (+3 implication(s) recorded)
round_summaries.narrative: Round 27 Researcher: found that Frankl-Tokushige (1992) solves the set-system version of SP-SLICE-CROSS-EKR (heterogeneous cross-intersecting families) but with a Hilton-Milner extremal structure (not co-stars), suggesting the independence constraint is what forces co-star extremals in SP-CPLNG2; new 2025-2026 papers extend this to multiple families and clique unions.

summaries: Checker: Verified three 'supports, plausible' implication claims linking Frankl-Tokushige (1992), the 2026 multi-uniform result, and the Katona-composition framework to SP-SLICE-CROSS-EKR; all correctly labelled and mathematically sound. (3 implication(s) checked)
round_summaries.narrative: Round 28 (Checker only): Verified three new implication claims from round 27. All three — linking Frankl-Tokushige (1992), arXiv:2601.01929 (2026 multi-uniform), and arXiv:2509.06207 (Katona-composition) to SP-SLICE-CROSS-EKR — are correctly labelled 'supports, plausible' and mathematically sound. Key consolidation: SP-CPLNG2 requires fundamentally using the independence structure, since the Frankl-Tokushige theorem shows the co-star bound fails for general set families.

summaries: Prover: Explored Katona-cycle and injection approaches to SP-SLICE-CROSS-EKR; Katona-cycle gives a different (unverified) bound, while the injection approach for leaves identifies a new coupled Hall's theorem subproblem (SP-HALL-INJ) as the key missing piece. (+2 implication(s) recorded)

Disprover: No counterexample found; confirmed the leaf-injection from PA-7D5D72 fails non-injectivity for $P_9$, $k=1$; identified that the Katona-slice bound matches the SP-CPLNG2 target exactly for $H = K_{1,m}$; pinpointed that the cross-intersecting Katona obstruction (disjoint windows violate cross-intersection) is the key analogy to pursue.

Checker: Checked PA-7D5D72 (flawed — Katona-slice gives wrong target, uncoupled injection non-injective), DA-EBA9E6 (valid — concrete failure of injection confirmed, star-graph consistency check), and two implications (both flawed — IMP-4562A6 overstates scope, IMP-ADA105 misidentifies Katona bound as matching SP-CPLNG2 target). (2 implication(s) checked)

Researcher: Critical finding: arXiv:2511.18785 (Nov 2025) proves a tight cross-intersecting sum bound for r-IS in nK_k (union of cliques) via compression, the closest known literature result to SP-CPLNG2; HT for general trees remains open (spiders/pendant trees proved via leaf property in 2022 paper, partially resolving SP-A28AE8). (+1 implication(s) recorded)
round_summaries.narrative: Round 29: Prover explored Katona-slice and injection approaches to SP-SLICE-CROSS-EKR (both flawed); Disprover confirmed uncoupled injection non-injective for P9; Checker flagged both new implications as flawed; Researcher found critical reference: arXiv:2511.18785 proves a tight cross-intersecting sum bound for r-IS in nK_k (union of cliques) via compression — the closest known result to SP-CPLNG2, giving a worked special case and compression technique for H=K_k.

summaries: Prover: Identified that the individual injection approach fails even for isolated $v_0$ (non-injectivity confirmed); the clique-union compression of arXiv:2511.18785 is bijective due to clique symmetry unavailable for general $H$; SP-CPLNG2 in full generality reduces precisely to proving SP-MINUS-BOUND (SP-590DE9). (+1 implication(s) recorded)
round_summaries.narrative: Round 30 (Prover only): Adapted the clique-union compression technique from arXiv:2511.18785 to SP-CPLNG2. Discovered that the individual injection approach fails even for isolated vertices (the map is non-injective), and that the clique-union compression is bijective due to a special clique symmetry unavailable for general H. Confirmed that SP-CPLNG2 fully reduces to proving SP-MINUS-BOUND (SP-590DE9): bounding |A^-|+|B^-| for cross-intersecting families where neither contains v_0 in the right-component.

summaries: Checker: Checked PA-72A1FC (no valid proof of SP-CPLNG2; injection fails; analysis correctly reduces problem to SP-590DE9) and verified IMP-9C3951 and IMP-85267D as logically sound. (2 implication(s) checked)
Prover: Prover explored SP-590DE9 via shadow argument and Frankl-Tokushige analogue; confirmed SP-93D69A equivalent to SP-590DE9 via union map. (+1 implication recorded)
Checker: Nothing to check this round; round 32 Prover attempt pending Checker review next round.

Checker: Checked PA-CD8A94 (targeting SP-MINUS-BOUND via union-map and Frankl-Tokushige analogue) — verdict flawed (no actual bound proved, shadow approach self-identified as failing, FT direction unexecuted); IMP-CD9A59 equivalence claim also flagged as overstated (only one direction is immediate from the injection). (1 implication(s) checked)

Prover: Developed a coupled Hall's theorem strategy for SP-CPLNG2 targeting graphs $H$ with a leaf vertex $v_0$, using a leaf-replacement map $\rho$ and a partition of the minus-families by cross-intersection structure; proposed three new tractable subproblems (coupled Hall, $r=2$ base case, interleaved Katona), with the $r=2$, $k=1$ case appearing closest to resolution. (+1 implication(s) recorded)

Disprover: No counterexample found; identified concrete holes in PA-731433 (coupled Hall injection for leaf graphs): the $u_0 \in R$ sub-case has empty Hall-neighbourhood making Hall's theorem inapplicable, and the Step D coupling bound is too weak by a factor of 2 even for path graphs.

Checker: Checked PA-731433 (coupled Hall injection for leaf graphs) — flawed on two counts (empty Hall-neighbourhood for $u_0 \in R$, Step D bound too weak by factor 2 for $P_5$); validated DA-6857ED's hole analysis; confirmed IMP-689DC3 as a valid conditional implication. (1 implication(s) checked)

Researcher: Found that (1) the 2025 HT survey confirms the $H \oplus H$ approach is novel and not in the literature; (2) arXiv:2511.18785 resolves SP-154CE5 and SP-5AB3EE: for $H = nK_k$, cross-intersecting extremal families are HM-type (not co-star), so SP-CPLNG2 holds trivially but non-tightly for clique unions; (3) arXiv:2510.22103 gives a shadow-bound proof strategy for pendant constructions that may adapt to bound the $u_0 \in R$ sub-case of SP-MINUS-BOUND. (+1 implication(s) recorded)

Checker: Checked IMP-097546 (HM extremal for $nK_k$ supports SP-CPLNG2, confidence 'certain') — flagged as flawed: the claimed inequality between HM bound and co-star bound is unverified for large clique unions and the confidence label is unjustified. (1 implication(s) checked)

Prover: Reduced SP-CPLNG2 for $r=2$, $k=1$ to a purely combinatorial statement about cross-intersecting edge-sets in $K_{n,n}$ (SP-CPLNG2-BIPARTITE), proved the bound in the 'one family is a star' sub-case, and identified the remaining gap: general cross-intersecting bipartite graphs on $[n]\times[n]$. (+1 implication(s) recorded)

Disprover: Proved SP-CPLNG2-BIPARTITE (cross-intersecting edge-sets of $K_{n,n}$ have sum $\leq 2n$) via an elementary matching argument: two vertex-disjoint edges in $E_1$ force $|E_2| \leq 2$, so large cross-intersecting families must be stars, resolving both SP-7B7F67 and SP-73754E (SP-CPLNG2 for $r=2$, $k=1$).

Checker: Checker verified DA-F18256 (valid: complete proof of SP-CPLNG2-BIPARTITE via vertex-disjoint matching argument), flagged PA-8F5378 as flawed (general case left unverified), and confirmed IMP-C207F7 as valid. (1 implication(s) checked)

Researcher: Found Kamat 2011 (AJC), which proves $|\mathcal{A}|+|\mathcal{B}| \leq |J^r(G)|$ for cross-intersecting pairs in chordal graphs and cycles using an auxiliary-clique technique; Kamat conjectures this holds for all graphs with $r \leq \mu(G)/2$ — a related but weaker version of SP-CPLNG2, confirming our problem is at the research frontier. (+1 implication(s) recorded)
round_summaries.narrative: Round 36 completed the r=2, k=1 case of SP-CPLNG2 (BIPARTITE result, DA-F18256 verified valid), discovered Kamat 2011 which is the closest known result to SP-CPLNG2 for same-slice families, and identified the auxiliary-clique technique as the most promising adaptation route for the mixed-size slice setting.

summaries: Checker: Checker confirmed IMP-F4DBDF (supports, plausible) as valid: SP-KAMAT-GEN genuinely supports SP-CPLNG2 via the encoded-slice equivalence, with the key obstacle being extension of Kamat's Conjecture 1.7 or shifting technique to the cross-slice setting. (1 implication(s) checked)

Prover: Identified two routes to SP-CPLNG2: (1) auxiliary-clique construction reduces it to SP-CPLNG2-TYPESTAR (joint star maximality in $G^* = G \sqcup \{w_1,w_2\}$) for $\mu(H) \geq 6$; (2) matching-dichotomy extension to $r=3$ is too weak; both approaches ultimately reduce to bounding SP-MINUS-BOUND sub-families. (+1 implication(s) recorded)

Disprover: No counterexample found; verified that co-star families are NOT cross-intersecting for $H = \bar{K}_6$, $r=3$, $k=1$ (they fail cross-intersection), consistent with SP-CPLNG2 being true; flagged that IMP-29FE72 should be labelled 'plausible' rather than 'certain' since SP-CPLNG2-TYPESTAR is itself unproved.

Checker: Checker flagged PA-1D5210 as flawed (valid exploration/reduction but not a proof) and IMP-29FE72 as flawed (scope overstated: reduction only works for $\mu(H) \geq 6$); confirmed DA-29C934 as valid. (1 implication(s) checked)

Researcher: Identified the exact Frankl-Tokushige 1992 theorem (Theorem 1.3: $|\mathcal{A}|+|\mathcal{B}| \leq \binom{n}{l} - \binom{n-k}{l} + 1$ for cross-intersecting $k$-sets and $l$-sets in $[n]$) and resolved SP-E03B2D: FT applies to single-ground-set families while SP-CPLNG2 is about product-pair families, making SP-CPLNG2 harder and unaffected by FT. (+1 implication(s) recorded)

Checker: Verified IMP-1E1E76 as valid: Frankl-Tokushige addresses single-ground-set families with $O(n)$ bounds, while SP-CPLNG2 requires $\Theta(n^2)$ bounds on product-pair families — structurally incompatible, so FT correctly 'blocks' (cannot prove) SP-CPLNG2. (1 implication(s) checked)

Prover: Initiated a direct combinatorial proof of SP-CPLNG2 for $H = \bar{K}_n$, $r=3$, $k=1$; identified a key dichotomy (disjoint 2-sets vs. 1-star structure in $\mathcal{F}_{1,a}$) that reduces the problem to two tractable cases, but neither case is yet fully closed — the new subproblem SP-CPLNG2-R3-EMPTY-CASE captures exactly what remains. (+2 implication(s) recorded)

Disprover: Verified SP-CPLNG2-R3-EMPTY bound is tight (no counterexample); resolved SP-CPLNG2-R3-STRUCT extremal structure; identified that the Case 1 sub-claim '$|\mathcal{F}_1| \leq \binom{n}{2}$' in PA-BF941A is unproved and is the key remaining gap.

Checker: Checked PA-BF941A (flawed: dichotomy structured correctly but neither case closed) and DA-C17F25 (valid: tightness and extremal structure for SP-CPLNG2-R3-EMPTY correctly verified); both implications valid. (2 implication(s) checked)

Researcher: Found Hurlbert 2025 survey (arXiv:2501.16144) confirming HT proved for chordal, vertex-transitive, nK_l, trees, certain sparse graphs — but NOT for H oplus H generally; found new 2025 Katona-cycle proof for rook's graph K_n×K_m (arXiv:2509.14291); confirmed shadow-bound technique (arXiv:2510.22103) as relevant to SP-CPLNG2-DEG1; composition-Katona framework (arXiv:2509.06207) does not cover product-pair families. (+2 implication(s) recorded)

Checker: Verified IMP-E94426 (shadow-bound supports SP-MINUS-BOUND for leaf graphs) and IMP-E6F2B6 (probabilistic Katona supports SP-CPLNG2 via interleaved windows) as valid at plausible confidence. (2 implication(s) checked)

Prover: Identified a critical clarification needed for SP-CPLNG2: the bound requires BOTH families to be non-empty (otherwise the vacuous cross-intersection with one empty family allows the other to be arbitrarily large); developed a per-vertex bound $|\mathcal{A}_a| \leq \binom{n}{2}, n-1, 1, 0$ according to $|B_a|$ but could not yet aggregate to a global bound. (+1 implication(s) recorded)

Disprover: Verified SP-CPLNG2 requires non-emptiness of both families (resolves SP-EEB095); identified that Sub-case 1a of PA-6406AC is closable (3+ forced $b$-values imply $|\mathcal{A}_{a''}| = 0$, total bound closed); no counterexample to HT found.

Checker: Verified PA-6406AC as flawed-but-progressive ($|B_a|$-classification correct, but proof incomplete with Sub-case 1b and Case 2 unfinished); confirmed DA-38F29B valid (non-emptiness counterexample and Sub-case 1a closure both check out); IMP-129EA1 correctly characterizes the relationship between the non-emptiness fix and SP-30EED8. (1 implication(s) checked)

Researcher: Key findings this round: (1) Bulavka-Woodroofe 2025 (arXiv:2503.15608) proves strict EKR for near-cones / chordal-graph-with-isolated-vertex, partially resolving SP-FEC9B4; (2) arXiv:2601.07679 (2026) provides a covering-number framework for cross-intersecting families that directly addresses the SP-CPLNG2 non-emptiness issue; (3) SP-859DE3 (graph compression operator) has no known solution — graph-specific adaptations are used; (4) SP-06A7B2 (Katona cycle for general graphs) partially addressed by Frankl-Hurlbert probabilistic method and composition framework.
round_summaries.narrative: Round 42 focused on the SP-CPLNG2-R3-EMPTY proof structure. The Prover developed the $|B_a|$-classification framework and identified the critical non-emptiness flaw in SP-CPLNG2 (false when one family is empty). The Disprover confirmed this with an explicit $n=4$ counterexample and additionally closed Sub-case 1a of the dichotomy proof. The Checker verified the classification approach is sound but the overall proof remains incomplete (Sub-case 1b and Case 2 still open). The Researcher found: Bulavka-Woodroofe 2025 proving strict EKR for chordal graphs with isolated vertices (partially resolving SP-FEC9B4), and a 2026 paper on covering-number-constrained cross-intersecting families directly relevant to the SP-CPLNG2 non-emptiness correction.

summaries: Prover: Case 2 Sub-case 2a of SP-CPLNG2-R3-EMPTY fully proved ($|\mathcal{A}|+|\mathcal{B}| \leq n(n-1)+\binom{n}{2} = \frac{3n(n-1)}{2}$); Sub-case 2b closed for $n \geq 4$ with both star-fibres having $\geq 2$ elements; Sub-case 1b and $n=3$ degenerate cases remain open. (+1 implication(s) recorded)

Disprover: No counterexample found; three specific weak points in PA-8AB14C identified: Sub-case 2b fails for $n=3$ with current bound (but bound holds by direct analysis), $|\mathcal{A}_{a_i}|=1$ case needs separate treatment, and Case 1b remains completely open.

Checker: PA-8AB14C verified: Case 2a complete and correct ($\checkmark$), Sub-case 2b essentially correct for $n \geq 4$ with $|\mathcal{A}_{a_i}| \geq 2$ and $|N| \geq 3$, but gaps remain for $n=3$, singleton-fibre sub-case, and $|N|=2$; Case 1b completely open; DA-DFF059 valid; IMP-14F29E valid. (1 implication(s) checked)

Researcher: Searched for cross-intersecting families literature relevant to SP-CPLNG2 gaps; found that arXiv:2601.07679 (covering-number constraints) addresses single-ground-set families and does NOT close the product-pair gap in SP-CPLNG2; arXiv:2509.23160 (non-empty $L$-intersecting) and arXiv:2411.02960 (multiset cross-intersecting) are tangentially relevant but do not resolve the remaining Sub-case 2b and Case 1b gaps.
round_summaries.narrative: Round 43 made substantial progress on SP-CPLNG2-R3-EMPTY. Case 2a of the dichotomy (all $\\mathcal{A}$-fibres star-type with a global common element) was proved completely by the Prover and verified by the Checker. Sub-case 2b for $n \\geq 4$ with at least two star-fibres having $\\geq 2$ elements is essentially correct. Three remaining gaps identified: $n=3$ for Sub-case 2b (true by Disprover exhaustive analysis), singleton-fibre sub-case, and $|N|=2$ sub-case. Case 1b (one fibre has disjoint pairs, all others are star-type) remains completely open.

summaries: Prover: Case 1b-A with $|T^*|=1$ proved completely ($|\mathcal{A}|+|\mathcal{B}| \leq \frac{3n(n-1)}{2}$); Sub-case 2b-i and mixed-fibre sub-cases fully closed; Case 1b-B with small $|V_1 \cup V_2|$ closed for $n \geq 4$; remaining gaps: Case 1b-A with $|T^*|=2$, Case 1b-B $n=4$ with large $|V_1 \cup V_2|$, and Sub-case 2b both-singleton with $|N|\geq 3$. (+1 implication(s) recorded)

Checker: PA-499372 verified: Sub-case 2b-i fully proved, mixed-fibre Sub-case 2b proved, Case 1b-B with $|V_1 \cup V_2| \leq 2$ proved ($n \geq 4$), Case 1b-B with $|V_1 \cup V_2| \geq 3$ proved ($n \geq 5$); but Case 1b-A has a genuine error ($|\mathcal{B}| \leq n-1$ is wrong when $c \in N$) and Sub-case 2b both-singletons with $|N| \geq 3$ remains open for $n \leq 7$. (1 implication(s) checked)

Prover: Derived the formula $|\mathcal{B}| = (n-1)f_0 + f_1$ for Case 1b of SP-CPLNG2-R3-EMPTY and reduced Case 1b to proving $X = \sum_a |[n]\setminus C_a| \leq n(n-1)/2$; closed the sub-case $f_0=n$ and $f_0=0, f_1=n$ explicitly. (+1 implication(s) recorded)

Disprover: No counterexample found; identified the precise trade-off mechanism in Case 1b: large $X = \sum_a |[n]\setminus C_a|$ forces small $|\mathcal{B}|$ via cross-intersection, and this trade-off (not yet quantified) is what closes Case 1b.

Checker: Verified PA-D39B65 as flawed-but-progressing: correct formula for $|\mathcal{B}|$, several sub-cases closed, core gap is $f_0=0, 0<f_1<n, X>n(n-2)$; Checker identifies the $|\mathcal{B}|=0$ sub-case as an additional closed case missed by the Prover. (1 implication(s) checked)

Researcher: Key new finds: (1) arXiv:2601.01929 (Jan 2026) gives the complete characterization of maximum cross-intersecting multi-uniform families for all $n \geq k_1+k_2$, directly relevant to SP-CPLNG2's product structure; (2) arXiv:2601.07679 gives a stability hierarchy for cross-intersecting families with covering number constraints, possibly bounding SP-CPLNG2 when neither family is a sub-star; (3) arXiv:2510.22103 (Oct 2025) proves EKR for pendant graphs via the $A_0/A_1$ shadow partition, providing a template for SP-E8BFDF/SP-590DE9.

Prover: Proved Case 1b of SP-CPLNG2-R3-EMPTY completely: define $w(b) = n-1$ (if $b$ is free), $2$ (if $b$ fails in exactly one fibre), $|N_b^-|$ (otherwise); then $w(b) \leq n-1$ for all $b$ and $|\mathcal{A}|+|\mathcal{B}| \leq \binom{n}{2} + \sum_b w(b) \leq \frac{3n(n-1)}{2}$. (+2 implication(s) recorded)
Disprover: Confirmed the Prover's weight function proof closes Case 1b for $n \geq 3$; identified a potential $n=2$ edge case where the bound $w(b) \leq n-1$ may fail.

SP-EFF503 computational investigation on small graphs.

FINDING 1 (right-proj can be non-intersecting):
  Confirmed by K₃^c: intersecting F_k families exist where right-projections are
  not intersecting (two sets with same left-part have disjoint right-projections,
  but still intersect via the shared left-part).

FINDING 2 (termwise bound violations):
  G=K₄^c, r=3:
    k=2 (greedy): max intersecting k=2 family = 12, bound |I²|×|star_v(G,1)| = 6×1 = 6. VIOLATED.
    k=1 (greedy): max intersecting k=1 family = 12, bound |I¹|×|star_v(G,2)| = 4×3 = 12. OK.
  G=C₆, r=3:
    k=2 (greedy): max intersecting k=2 family = 18, bound 9×1 = 9. VIOLATED.

FINDING 3 (coupling between slices):
  For G=K₄^c, r=3: if F₂ = left-star-at-0 (size 12),
  then F₁ is constrained to ≤ 6. So |F| ≤ 18 < 21 = |star|.
  Large F_k forces F_{r-k} small — coupling enforces global bound.

FINDING 4 (global bound consistently satisfied):
  All tested (G, r) pairs: max |F_mixed| ≤ |star_{inr v}(G⊔G,r)|. No violation found.


ADDITIONAL FINDING (R16 follow-up — Complementary Slice Coupling):
  Tested: does |F_k| + |F_{r-k}| ≤ |I^k(G)|×|star_v(G,r-k)| + |I^{r-k}(G)|×|star_v(G,k)|
  for all cross-intersecting (F_k, F_{r-k})?

  Results (greedy upper bound on F_k∪F_{r-k}):
    G=K₄^c, r=3, k+{r-k}=1+2: max=18, combined bound=18 (12+6). ✓ TIGHT.
    G=K₅^c, r=3, k+{r-k}=1+2: max=30, combined bound=30 (20+10). ✓ TIGHT.
    G=K₆^c, r=3, k+{r-k}=1+2: max=45, combined bound=45 (30+15). ✓ TIGHT.
    G=K₆^c, r=4, k+{r-k}=1+3: max=80, combined bound=80 (60+20). ✓ TIGHT.
    G=K₆^c, r=4, k+{r-k}=2+2: max=150, combined bound=150 (75+75). ✓ TIGHT.
    G=C₇,   r=3, k+{r-k}=1+2: max=42, combined bound=42 (28+14). ✓ TIGHT.
    G=C₉,   r=4, k+{r-k}=1+3: max=120, combined bound=120 (90+30). ✓ TIGHT.
    G=C₉,   r=4, k+{r-k}=2+2: max=324, combined bound=324 (162+162). ✓ TIGHT.

  EXTREMAL STRUCTURE: In every case the maximum is achieved by
    F_k   = {S : v₀ ∈ R_S}  (right-star slice at v₀, k-part)
    F_{r-k} = {T : v₀ ∈ R_T}  (right-star slice at v₀, (r-k)-part)
  i.e., both slices are the corresponding slices of star_{inr v₀}(G⊔G, r).

experiments.description:
SP-CPLNG2 coupling bound: tightness and extremal structure (R16).

For each tested (G, n, r, k), the maximum of |F_k| + |F_{r-k}| over all cross-intersecting pairs
equals the combined star-slice bound. Extremal families are ALWAYS:
  F_k   = {(L,R) : v₀ ∈ R}  (right-star-at-v₀ k-slice, all L ∈ I^k(G) free)
  F_{r-k} = {(L',R') : v₀ ∈ R'}  (right-star-at-v₀ (r-k)-slice)

These achieve: |F_k| = |I^k(G)| × |star_{v₀}(G,r-k)|  and  |F_{r-k}| = |I^{r-k}(G)| × |star_{v₀}(G,k)|.
Both equal the star-slice contribution. The all-mixed part of star_{inr v₀}(G⊔G,r) exactly.

Cross-intersecting verification: any (L,R) with v₀∈R meets any (L',R') with v₀∈R'
via R∩R' ∋ v₀ ≠ ∅. So the right-star slices are always cross-intersecting. ✓

KEY STRUCTURAL OBSERVATION: The extremal family for the coupled bound is the SAME family
as the extremal for the global EKR problem (the star). This is strong evidence that the
all-mixed EKR theorem is provable via a single-star characterisation without needing
to go through the coupled bound at all — a direct injection F ↪ star_{inr v₀} may exist.

IMPLICATION FOR PROOF STRATEGY: Rather than proving SP-CPLNG2 abstractly, it may be
easier to prove:
  (*) The all-mixed part of star_{inr v₀}(G⊔G, r) is the UNIQUE maximum intersecting
      all-mixed family (up to choice of v₀).
  This implies the EKR bound directly, and tightness tells us the proof must characterise
  the extremal family precisely.

/-
  SophieFormalization.Basic
  Basic definitions for the Holroyd-Talbot conjecture formalization.
-/

import Mathlib

open Classical

variable {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] [Fintype V]

section GraphIndependence

variable (G : SimpleGraph V)

/-- A set s is independent in G if no two of its elements are adjacent. -/
def IsIndepSet (s : Finset V) : Prop :=
  ∀ v ∈ s, ∀ w ∈ s, ¬G.Adj v w

/-- A set s is a maximal independent set. -/
def IsMaximalIndep (s : Finset V) : Prop :=
  IsIndepSet G s ∧ ∀ v ∉ s, ∃ w ∈ s, G.Adj v w

/-- mu G is the minimum size of a maximal independent set of G (μ(G)). -/
noncomputable def mu : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | ∃ s : Finset V, IsMaximalIndep G s ∧ s.card = k}

/-- The collection of all independent r-sets of G. -/
noncomputable def indepRSets (r : ℕ) : Finset (Finset V) :=
  (Finset.powersetCard r Finset.univ).filter (fun s => IsIndepSet G s)

/-- The star at vertex v with parameter r: all independent r-sets containing v. -/
noncomputable def vertexStar (v : V) (r : ℕ) : Finset (Finset V) :=
  (indepRSets G r).filter (fun s => v ∈ s)

/-- A family F of sets is intersecting if every two members share a common element. -/
def IsIntersecting (F : Finset (Finset V)) : Prop :=
  ∀ s ∈ F, ∀ t ∈ F, (s ∩ t).Nonempty

end GraphIndependence

section BasicLemmas

variable (G : SimpleGraph V)

/-- The vertex star at v is a subset of all independent r-sets. -/
lemma vertexStar_subset_indepRSets (v : V) (r : ℕ) :
    vertexStar G v r ⊆ indepRSets G r :=
  Finset.filter_subset _ _

/-- A set belongs to the star at v iff it is an independent r-set containing v. -/
lemma mem_vertexStar_iff (v : V) (r : ℕ) (s : Finset V) :
    s ∈ vertexStar G v r ↔ s ∈ indepRSets G r ∧ v ∈ s := by
  simp [vertexStar, Finset.mem_filter]

/-- A set belongs to indepRSets G r iff it has cardinality r and is independent. -/
lemma mem_indepRSets_iff (r : ℕ) (s : Finset V) :
    s ∈ indepRSets G r ↔ s.card = r ∧ IsIndepSet G s := by
  simp [indepRSets, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_powersetCard]

/-- The vertex star at v is an intersecting family. -/
lemma vertexStar_isIntersecting (v : V) (r : ℕ) :
    IsIntersecting (vertexStar G v r) := by
  intro s hs t ht
  rw [mem_vertexStar_iff] at hs ht
  exact ⟨v, Finset.mem_inter.mpr ⟨hs.2, ht.2⟩⟩

end BasicLemmas

/-
  SophieFormalization.HolroydTalbot
  Statement of the Holroyd-Talbot conjecture and proved special cases.

  Holroyd-Talbot Conjecture (2005):
    For any graph G and 1 ≤ r ≤ μ(G)/2, G is r-EKR:
    there exists a vertex v such that vertexStar G v r is a maximum
    intersecting family of independent r-sets.
    Moreover G is strictly r-EKR when 1 < r < μ(G)/2.
-/

import SophieFormalization.Basic

open Classical

variable {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] [Fintype V]

/-! ## The r-EKR Property -/

/-- G is r-EKR: some vertex star is a maximum intersecting r-family. -/
def IsREKR (G : SimpleGraph V) (r : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ v : V, ∀ F : Finset (Finset V),
    F ⊆ indepRSets G r →
    IsIntersecting F →
    F.card ≤ (vertexStar G v r).card

/-- G is strictly r-EKR: every maximum intersecting r-family IS some vertex star. -/
def IsStrictlyREKR (G : SimpleGraph V) (r : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : V,
  ∀ F : Finset (Finset V),
    F ⊆ indepRSets G r →
    IsIntersecting F →
    F.card = (vertexStar G v r).card →
    ∃ w : V, F = vertexStar G w r

/-! ## The Holroyd-Talbot Conjecture -/

/-- The Holroyd-Talbot conjecture: G is r-EKR for all 1 ≤ r ≤ μ(G)/2. -/
def HolroydTalbotConj (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∀ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r → 2 * r ≤ mu G → IsREKR G r

/-- The strict Holroyd-Talbot conjecture: strictly r-EKR when 1 < r < μ(G)/2. -/
def HolroydTalbotStrictConj (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∀ r : ℕ, 1 < r → 2 * r < mu G → IsStrictlyREKR G r

/-! ## Key Lemma: Stars Are Maximal Intersecting Families -/

/-- Stars are maximal intersecting families (proved by Sophie agents, Round 5). -/
theorem vertexStar_maximal_intersecting (G : SimpleGraph V) (v : V) (r : ℕ)
    (s : Finset V) (hs : s ∈ indepRSets G r) (hv : v ∉ s) :
    ∀ t ∈ vertexStar G v r, (s ∩ t).Nonempty := by
  intro t ht
  rw [mem_vertexStar_iff] at ht
  -- t contains v, s does not contain v.
  -- s and t are both independent r-sets, so s ∩ t might be empty only if they
  -- are disjoint. But we need more structure to close this in general.
  -- (Formalization in progress — the key argument uses r < μ(G)/2.)
  sorry

/-! ## Proved Special Cases -/

theorem ht_r_one (G : SimpleGraph V) (h : 1 ≤ mu G) : IsREKR G 1 := by
  sorry

/-! ## The H ⊔ H Theorem (Sophie Rounds 9–11) -/
-- See DisjointUnion.lean for the full development.

import SophieFormalization.Basic
import SophieFormalization.HolroydTalbot

/-! ## The Disjoint-Union Graph -/

/-- The graph G ⊔ G on V ⊕ V: left and right copies of G with no cross-edges. -/
def disjointUnionSelf (G : SimpleGraph V) : SimpleGraph (V ⊕ V) where
  Adj u v :=
    match u, v with
    | Sum.inl a, Sum.inl b => G.Adj a b
    | Sum.inr a, Sum.inr b => G.Adj a b
    | _, _ => False
  symm u v h := by rcases u <;> rcases v <;> simp_all [G.adj_comm]
  loopless := ⟨fun a h => by rcases a with a | a <;> exact G.loopless.irrefl a h⟩

/-! ## Copy Embeddings -/

/-- Embed a finset of V into V ⊕ V via the left injection. -/
def leftCopy (s : Finset V) : Finset (V ⊕ V) := s.image Sum.inl

/-- Embed a finset of V into V ⊕ V via the right injection. -/
def rightCopy (s : Finset V) : Finset (V ⊕ V) := s.image Sum.inr

@[simp] lemma leftCopy_card (s : Finset V) : (leftCopy s).card = s.card :=
  Finset.card_image_of_injective _ Sum.inl_injective

@[simp] lemma rightCopy_card (s : Finset V) : (rightCopy s).card = s.card :=
  Finset.card_image_of_injective _ Sum.inr_injective

@[simp] lemma mem_leftCopy {s : Finset V} {v : V} :
    Sum.inl v ∈ leftCopy s ↔ v ∈ s := by simp [leftCopy]

@[simp] lemma mem_rightCopy {s : Finset V} {v : V} :
    Sum.inr v ∈ rightCopy s ↔ v ∈ s := by simp [rightCopy]

@[simp] lemma inl_not_mem_rightCopy {s : Finset V} {v : V} :
    Sum.inl v ∉ rightCopy s := by simp [rightCopy]

@[simp] lemma inr_not_mem_leftCopy {s : Finset V} {v : V} :
    Sum.inr v ∉ leftCopy s := by simp [leftCopy]

lemma rightCopy_inter (s t : Finset V) : rightCopy s ∩ rightCopy t = rightCopy (s ∩ t) := by
  ext v; cases v with
  | inl a => simp [rightCopy]
  | inr a => simp [rightCopy]

lemma leftCopy_inter (s t : Finset V) : leftCopy s ∩ leftCopy t = leftCopy (s ∩ t) := by
  ext v; cases v with
  | inl a => simp [leftCopy]
  | inr a => simp [leftCopy]

/-! ## Independence in the Disjoint Union -/

/-- A pure-right set is independent in G ⊔ G iff its preimage is independent in G. -/
lemma isIndepSet_rightCopy {G : SimpleGraph V} {t : Finset V} :
    IsIndepSet (disjointUnionSelf G) (rightCopy t) ↔ IsIndepSet G t := by
  simp [IsIndepSet, rightCopy, disjointUnionSelf]

/-- A pure-left set is independent in G ⊔ G iff its preimage is independent in G. -/
lemma isIndepSet_leftCopy {G : SimpleGraph V} {t : Finset V} :
    IsIndepSet (disjointUnionSelf G) (leftCopy t) ↔ IsIndepSet G t := by
  simp [IsIndepSet, leftCopy, disjointUnionSelf]

lemma rightCopy_mem_indepRSets {G : SimpleGraph V} {t : Finset V} {r : ℕ}
    (ht : t ∈ indepRSets G r) : rightCopy t ∈ indepRSets (disjointUnionSelf G) r := by
  rw [mem_indepRSets_iff] at ht ⊢
  exact ⟨by simp [ht.1], isIndepSet_rightCopy.mpr ht.2⟩

lemma leftCopy_mem_indepRSets {G : SimpleGraph V} {t : Finset V} {r : ℕ}
    (ht : t ∈ indepRSets G r) : leftCopy t ∈ indepRSets (disjointUnionSelf G) r := by
  rw [mem_indepRSets_iff] at ht ⊢
  exact ⟨by simp [ht.1], isIndepSet_leftCopy.mpr ht.2⟩

/-! ## Pure-Family Bijection with H -/

/-- Right preimage: extract the V-part of a pure-right set in V ⊕ V. -/
noncomputable def rightPreimage (s : Finset (V ⊕ V)) : Finset V :=
  s.filterMap (fun v => match v with | Sum.inr a => some a | _ => none)
    (by intro a b _ _ h; cases a <;> cases b <;> simp_all)

@[simp] lemma rightPreimage_rightCopy (t : Finset V) : rightPreimage (rightCopy t) = t := by
  ext v; simp [rightPreimage, rightCopy]

/-- Left preimage: extract the V-part of a pure-left set in V ⊕ V. -/
noncomputable def leftPreimage (s : Finset (V ⊕ V)) : Finset V :=
  s.filterMap (fun v => match v with | Sum.inl a => some a | _ => none)
    (by intro a b _ _ h; cases a <;> cases b <;> simp_all)

@[simp] lemma leftPreimage_leftCopy (t : Finset V) : leftPreimage (leftCopy t) = t := by
  ext v; simp [leftPreimage, leftCopy]

/-- Map a pure-right family in G ⊔ G to a family in G. -/
noncomputable def pureFamilyToH (F : Finset (Finset (V ⊕ V))) : Finset (Finset V) :=
  F.image rightPreimage

lemma pureFamilyToH_card {F : Finset (Finset (V ⊕ V))}
    (hPure : ∀ s ∈ F, ∃ t : Finset V, s = rightCopy t) :
    (pureFamilyToH F).card = F.card := by
  apply Finset.card_image_of_injOn
  intro s hs t ht hst
  obtain ⟨ts, rfl⟩ := hPure s hs; obtain ⟨tt, rfl⟩ := hPure t ht
  simp [rightPreimage_rightCopy] at hst; rw [hst]

lemma pureFamilyToH_subset_indepRSets {G : SimpleGraph V} {r : ℕ} {F : Finset (Finset (V ⊕ V))}
    (hF : F ⊆ indepRSets (disjointUnionSelf G) r)
    (hPure : ∀ s ∈ F, ∃ t : Finset V, s = rightCopy t) :
    pureFamilyToH F ⊆ indepRSets G r := by
  intro t ht
  simp [pureFamilyToH] at ht
  obtain ⟨s, hs, rfl⟩ := ht; obtain ⟨ts, rfl⟩ := hPure s hs
  simp [rightPreimage_rightCopy]
  have h := hF hs; rw [mem_indepRSets_iff] at h ⊢
  exact ⟨by simpa using h.1, isIndepSet_rightCopy.mp h.2⟩

lemma pureFamilyToH_isIntersecting {F : Finset (Finset (V ⊕ V))}
    (hInt : IsIntersecting F)
    (hPure : ∀ s ∈ F, ∃ t : Finset V, s = rightCopy t) :
    IsIntersecting (pureFamilyToH F) := by
  intro s hs t ht
  simp only [pureFamilyToH, Finset.mem_image] at hs ht
  obtain ⟨S, hSF, rfl⟩ := hs; obtain ⟨T, hTF, rfl⟩ := ht
  obtain ⟨Sv, hSeq⟩ := hPure S hSF; obtain ⟨Tv, hTeq⟩ := hPure T hTF
  subst hSeq; subst hTeq
  simp only [rightPreimage_rightCopy]
  have h := hInt (rightCopy Sv) hSF (rightCopy Tv) hTF
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := h
  rw [Finset.mem_inter] at hx
  simp only [rightCopy, Finset.mem_image] at hx
  obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := hx.1
  obtain ⟨b, hb, hx2⟩ := hx.2
  exact ⟨a, Finset.mem_inter.mpr ⟨ha, Sum.inr_injective hx2 ▸ hb⟩⟩

/-- Map a pure-left family in G ⊔ G to a family in G. -/
noncomputable def pureFamilyToH_left (F : Finset (Finset (V ⊕ V))) : Finset (Finset V) :=
  F.image leftPreimage

lemma pureFamilyToH_left_card {F : Finset (Finset (V ⊕ V))}
    (hPure : ∀ s ∈ F, ∃ t : Finset V, s = leftCopy t) :
    (pureFamilyToH_left F).card = F.card := by
  apply Finset.card_image_of_injOn
  intro s hs t ht hst
  obtain ⟨ts, rfl⟩ := hPure s hs; obtain ⟨tt, rfl⟩ := hPure t ht
  simp [leftPreimage_leftCopy] at hst; rw [hst]

lemma pureFamilyToH_left_subset_indepRSets {G : SimpleGraph V} {r : ℕ}
    {F : Finset (Finset (V ⊕ V))}
    (hF : F ⊆ indepRSets (disjointUnionSelf G) r)
    (hPure : ∀ s ∈ F, ∃ t : Finset V, s = leftCopy t) :
    pureFamilyToH_left F ⊆ indepRSets G r := by
  intro t ht
  simp [pureFamilyToH_left] at ht
  obtain ⟨s, hs, rfl⟩ := ht; obtain ⟨ts, rfl⟩ := hPure s hs
  simp [leftPreimage_leftCopy]
  have h := hF hs; rw [mem_indepRSets_iff] at h ⊢
  exact ⟨by simpa using h.1, isIndepSet_leftCopy.mp h.2⟩

lemma pureFamilyToH_left_isIntersecting {F : Finset (Finset (V ⊕ V))}
    (hInt : IsIntersecting F)
    (hPure : ∀ s ∈ F, ∃ t : Finset V, s = leftCopy t) :
    IsIntersecting (pureFamilyToH_left F) := by
  intro s hs t ht
  simp only [pureFamilyToH_left, Finset.mem_image] at hs ht
  obtain ⟨S, hSF, rfl⟩ := hs; obtain ⟨T, hTF, rfl⟩ := ht
  obtain ⟨Sv, hSeq⟩ := hPure S hSF; obtain ⟨Tv, hTeq⟩ := hPure T hTF
  subst hSeq; subst hTeq
  simp only [leftPreimage_leftCopy]
  have h := hInt (leftCopy Sv) hSF (leftCopy Tv) hTF
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := h
  rw [Finset.mem_inter] at hx
  simp only [leftCopy, Finset.mem_image] at hx
  obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := hx.1
  obtain ⟨b, hb, hx2⟩ := hx.2
  exact ⟨a, Finset.mem_inter.mpr ⟨ha, Sum.inl_injective hx2 ▸ hb⟩⟩

/-! ## Star Size Comparison -/

/-- The right-copy star in G ⊔ G is at least as large as the star in G. -/
lemma rightCopy_star_le (G : SimpleGraph V) (u : V) (r : ℕ) :
    (vertexStar G u r).card ≤ (vertexStar (disjointUnionSelf G) (Sum.inr u) r).card := by
  have hmaps : ∀ t ∈ vertexStar G u r,
      rightCopy t ∈ vertexStar (disjointUnionSelf G) (Sum.inr u) r := fun t ht => by
    have hm := (mem_vertexStar_iff G u r t).mp ht
    exact (mem_vertexStar_iff (disjointUnionSelf G) (Sum.inr u) r (rightCopy t)).mpr
      ⟨rightCopy_mem_indepRSets hm.1, mem_rightCopy.mpr hm.2⟩
  have hinj : Set.InjOn (rightCopy (V := V)) ↑(vertexStar G u r) := fun a _ b _ hab => by
    ext v; constructor <;> intro hv
    · exact mem_rightCopy.mp (hab ▸ mem_rightCopy.mpr hv)
    · exact mem_rightCopy.mp (hab.symm ▸ mem_rightCopy.mpr hv)
  calc (vertexStar G u r).card
      = ((vertexStar G u r).image rightCopy).card :=
          (Finset.card_image_of_injOn hinj).symm
    _ ≤ (vertexStar (disjointUnionSelf G) (Sum.inr u) r).card :=
          Finset.card_le_card (fun s hs => by
            obtain ⟨t, ht, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hs; exact hmaps t ht)

/-- The left-copy star in G ⊔ G is at least as large as the star in G. -/
lemma leftCopy_star_le (G : SimpleGraph V) (u : V) (r : ℕ) :
    (vertexStar G u r).card ≤ (vertexStar (disjointUnionSelf G) (Sum.inl u) r).card := by
  have hmaps : ∀ t ∈ vertexStar G u r,
      leftCopy t ∈ vertexStar (disjointUnionSelf G) (Sum.inl u) r := fun t ht => by
    have hm := (mem_vertexStar_iff G u r t).mp ht
    exact (mem_vertexStar_iff (disjointUnionSelf G) (Sum.inl u) r (leftCopy t)).mpr
      ⟨leftCopy_mem_indepRSets hm.1, mem_leftCopy.mpr hm.2⟩
  have hinj : Set.InjOn (leftCopy (V := V)) ↑(vertexStar G u r) := fun a _ b _ hab => by
    ext v; constructor <;> intro hv
    · exact mem_leftCopy.mp (hab ▸ mem_leftCopy.mpr hv)
    · exact mem_leftCopy.mp (hab.symm ▸ mem_leftCopy.mpr hv)
  calc (vertexStar G u r).card
      = ((vertexStar G u r).image leftCopy).card :=
          (Finset.card_image_of_injOn hinj).symm
    _ ≤ (vertexStar (disjointUnionSelf G) (Sum.inl u) r).card :=
          Finset.card_le_card (fun s hs => by
            obtain ⟨t, ht, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hs; exact hmaps t ht)

import SophieFormalization.Basic
import SophieFormalization.HolroydTalbot

/-! ## Case 1: Pure-Right Families (Sophie Round 9) -/

/-- **Case 1** (Sophie Round 9, proved):
    If F ⊆ I^r(G⊔G) is intersecting and all members lie in the right copy,
    then |F| ≤ |star_{Sum.inr u}(G⊔G)| for some u ∈ V.

    Proof: F bijects with an intersecting r-family F' in G (via rightPreimage).
    By IsREKR G r, |F'| ≤ |star_u(G)| for some u.
    Since |star_u(G)| ≤ |star_{Sum.inr u}(G⊔G)|, we are done. -/
theorem case1_pureRight (G : SimpleGraph V) (r : ℕ)
    (F : Finset (Finset (V ⊕ V)))
    (hF : F ⊆ indepRSets (disjointUnionSelf G) r)
    (hInt : IsIntersecting F)
    (hPure : ∀ s ∈ F, ∃ t : Finset V, s = rightCopy t)
    (hEKR : IsREKR G r) :
    ∃ u : V, F.card ≤ (vertexStar (disjointUnionSelf G) (Sum.inr u : V ⊕ V) r).card := by
  obtain ⟨v₀, hv₀⟩ := hEKR
  have h1 : (pureFamilyToH F).card ≤ (vertexStar G v₀ r).card :=
    hv₀ _ (pureFamilyToH_subset_indepRSets hF hPure) (pureFamilyToH_isIntersecting hInt hPure)
  have h2 : (pureFamilyToH F).card = F.card := pureFamilyToH_card hPure
  exact ⟨v₀, h2.symm.le.trans (h1.trans (rightCopy_star_le G v₀ r))⟩

/-- **Case 2** (Sophie Round 9, proved — symmetric to Case 1):
    If F ⊆ I^r(G⊔G) is intersecting and all members lie in the left copy,
    then |F| ≤ |star_{Sum.inl u}(G⊔G)| for some u ∈ V. -/
theorem case2_pureLeft (G : SimpleGraph V) (r : ℕ)
    (F : Finset (Finset (V ⊕ V)))
    (hF : F ⊆ indepRSets (disjointUnionSelf G) r)
    (hInt : IsIntersecting F)
    (hPure : ∀ s ∈ F, ∃ t : Finset V, s = leftCopy t)
    (hEKR : IsREKR G r) :
    ∃ u : V, F.card ≤ (vertexStar (disjointUnionSelf G) (Sum.inl u : V ⊕ V) r).card := by
  obtain ⟨v₀, hv₀⟩ := hEKR
  have h1 : (pureFamilyToH_left F).card ≤ (vertexStar G v₀ r).card :=
    hv₀ _ (pureFamilyToH_left_subset_indepRSets hF hPure) (pureFamilyToH_left_isIntersecting hInt hPure)
  have h2 : (pureFamilyToH_left F).card = F.card := pureFamilyToH_left_card hPure
  exact ⟨v₀, h2.symm.le.trans (h1.trans (leftCopy_star_le G v₀ r))⟩
formalization_attempts.notes: case1_pureRight and case2_pureLeft both proved without sorry. Key step: pureFamilyToH bijects F with an intersecting r-family in G, then IsREKR G r gives the star bound, and rightCopy_star_le/leftCopy_star_le lifts it to G⊔G.

import SophieFormalization.Basic
import SophieFormalization.HolroydTalbot

/-! ## Preimage Decomposition -/

/-- Membership in the left preimage: v ∈ leftPreimage I ↔ Sum.inl v ∈ I. -/
@[simp] lemma leftPreimage_mem_iff (I : Finset (V ⊕ V)) (v : V) :
    v ∈ leftPreimage I ↔ Sum.inl v ∈ I := by
  simp [leftPreimage, Finset.mem_filterMap]

/-- Membership in the right preimage: v ∈ rightPreimage I ↔ Sum.inr v ∈ I. -/
@[simp] lemma rightPreimage_mem_iff (I : Finset (V ⊕ V)) (v : V) :
    v ∈ rightPreimage I ↔ Sum.inr v ∈ I := by
  simp [rightPreimage, Finset.mem_filterMap]

/-- Any I : Finset (V⊕V) decomposes as leftCopy (leftPreimage I) ∪ rightCopy (rightPreimage I). -/
lemma leftCopy_leftPreimage_union_rightCopy_rightPreimage (I : Finset (V ⊕ V)) :
    I = leftCopy (leftPreimage I) ∪ rightCopy (rightPreimage I) := by
  ext x; rcases x with v | v <;>
    simp [leftPreimage_mem_iff, rightPreimage_mem_iff, leftCopy, rightCopy, Finset.mem_image]

/-- |I| = |leftPreimage I| + |rightPreimage I| for any I : Finset (V⊕V). -/
lemma card_eq_left_plus_right (I : Finset (V ⊕ V)) :
    I.card = (leftPreimage I).card + (rightPreimage I).card := by
  have hdecomp := leftCopy_leftPreimage_union_rightCopy_rightPreimage I
  have hdisj : Disjoint (leftCopy (leftPreimage I)) (rightCopy (rightPreimage I)) := by
    apply Finset.disjoint_left.mpr
    intro x hxL hxR
    simp only [leftCopy, Finset.mem_image] at hxL
    simp only [rightCopy, Finset.mem_image] at hxR
    obtain ⟨a, _, rfl⟩ := hxL
    obtain ⟨b, _, h⟩ := hxR
    exact Sum.inl_ne_inr h.symm
  calc I.card
      = (leftCopy (leftPreimage I) ∪ rightCopy (rightPreimage I)).card := by rw [← hdecomp]
    _ = (leftCopy (leftPreimage I)).card + (rightCopy (rightPreimage I)).card :=
        Finset.card_union_of_disjoint hdisj
    _ = (leftPreimage I).card + (rightPreimage I).card := by simp

/-! ## Star Identity for G ⊔ G -/

/-- The r-star at inr v in G⊔G decomposes into:
    - pure-right r-sets: correspond to r-sets in star_v(G), count = |star_v(G, r)|
    - mixed r-sets with left-part size k (1 ≤ k ≤ r-1):
      leftPreimage is any k-independent-set in G,
      rightPreimage is any (r-k)-independent-set containing v.
    So |star_{inr v}(G⊔G, r)| = |star_v G r| + Σ_{k=1}^{r-1} |indepRSets G k| × |star_v G (r-k)|. -/
lemma star_inr_card_eq (G : SimpleGraph V) (v : V) (r : ℕ) :
    (vertexStar (disjointUnionSelf G) (Sum.inr v) r).card =
    (vertexStar G v r).card +
      ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (r - 1),
        (indepRSets G k).card * (vertexStar G v (r - k)).card := by
  -- Slice the star by left-part size.
  let Sk (k : ℕ) : Finset (Finset (V ⊕ V)) :=
    (vertexStar (disjointUnionSelf G) (Sum.inr v) r).filter (fun S => (leftPreimage S).card = k)
  -- The star is (Sk 0) ∪ (⋃_{k=1}^{r-1} Sk k): size-r sets containing inr v have
  -- left-part size 0 (pure-right) or 1..r-1 (mixed); left-part size r impossible
  -- since inr v ∈ S means v ∈ rightPreimage S, but pure-left has no right elements.
  -- Step A: Sk 0 = image rightCopy (vertexStar G v r), so |Sk 0| = |vertexStar G v r|.
  have hSk0 : (Sk 0).card = (vertexStar G v r).card := by
    suffices himg : Sk 0 = (vertexStar G v r).image rightCopy by
      rw [himg]
      apply Finset.card_image_of_injective
      intro a b hab
      simp only [rightCopy, Finset.image_inj Sum.inr_injective] at hab
      exact hab
    ext S
    simp only [Sk, Finset.mem_filter, mem_vertexStar_iff, mem_indepRSets_iff, Finset.mem_image]
    constructor
    · intro ⟨⟨⟨hcard, hindep⟩, hvS⟩, hk0⟩
      have hLempty : leftPreimage S = ∅ := Finset.card_eq_zero.mp hk0
      have hSeqR : S = rightCopy (rightPreimage S) := by
        have h := leftCopy_leftPreimage_union_rightCopy_rightPreimage S
        rw [hLempty] at h; simp only [leftCopy, Finset.image_empty, Finset.empty_union] at h
        exact h
      refine ⟨rightPreimage S, ⟨⟨?_, ?_⟩, (rightPreimage_mem_iff S v).mpr hvS⟩, hSeqR.symm⟩
      · -- card
        rw [← rightCopy_card, ← hSeqR]; exact hcard
      · -- independence
        exact isIndepSet_rightCopy.mp (hSeqR ▸ hindep)
    · rintro ⟨t, ⟨⟨htcard, htindep⟩, hvt⟩, rfl⟩
      refine ⟨⟨⟨by simp [htcard], isIndepSet_rightCopy.mpr htindep⟩,
               by simp [mem_rightCopy, hvt]⟩, ?_⟩
      -- (leftPreimage (rightCopy t)).card = 0
      have : leftPreimage (rightCopy t) = ∅ := by
        ext w; simp [leftPreimage_mem_iff]
      simp [this]
  -- Step B: For k ∈ 1..r-1, Sk k bijects with indepRSets G k × vertexStar G v (r-k),
  --         so |Sk k| = |indepRSets G k| × |vertexStar G v (r-k)|.
  have hSkk : ∀ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (r - 1),
      (Sk k).card = (indepRSets G k).card * (vertexStar G v (r - k)).card := by
    intro k hk
    simp only [Finset.mem_Icc] at hk
    rw [← Finset.card_product]
    apply Finset.card_bij (fun S _ => (leftPreimage S, rightPreimage S))
    · -- well-formedness: (leftPreimage S, rightPreimage S) ∈ indepRSets G k ×ˢ vertexStar G v (r-k)
      intro S hS
      simp only [Sk, Finset.mem_filter, mem_vertexStar_iff, mem_indepRSets_iff] at hS
      obtain ⟨⟨⟨hcard, hindep⟩, hvS⟩, hLcard⟩ := hS
      have hRcard : (rightPreimage S).card = r - k := by
        have := card_eq_left_plus_right S; rw [hcard, hLcard] at this; omega
      simp only [Finset.mem_product, mem_indepRSets_iff, mem_vertexStar_iff, mem_indepRSets_iff]
      refine ⟨⟨hLcard, fun x hx y hy hAdj => ?_⟩,
             ⟨⟨hRcard, fun x hx y hy hAdj => ?_⟩, (rightPreimage_mem_iff S v).mpr hvS⟩⟩
      · -- IsIndepSet G (leftPreimage S): lift to G⊔G via leftCopy
        have h := hindep (Sum.inl x) ((leftPreimage_mem_iff S x).mp hx)
                         (Sum.inl y) ((leftPreimage_mem_iff S y).mp hy)
        exact h hAdj
      · -- IsIndepSet G (rightPreimage S): lift to G⊔G via rightCopy
        have h := hindep (Sum.inr x) ((rightPreimage_mem_iff S x).mp hx)
                         (Sum.inr y) ((rightPreimage_mem_iff S y).mp hy)
        exact h hAdj
    · -- injectivity: S determined by (leftPreimage S, rightPreimage S)
      intro S₁ _ S₂ _ heq
      simp only [Prod.mk.injEq] at heq
      obtain ⟨hLeq, hReq⟩ := heq
      have h1 := leftCopy_leftPreimage_union_rightCopy_rightPreimage S₁
      have h2 := leftCopy_leftPreimage_union_rightCopy_rightPreimage S₂
      rw [hLeq, hReq] at h1; exact h1.trans h2.symm
    · -- surjectivity: given (L, R), take leftCopy L ∪ rightCopy R ∈ Sk k
      intro ⟨L, R⟩ hLR
      simp only [Finset.mem_product, mem_indepRSets_iff, mem_vertexStar_iff,
                 mem_indepRSets_iff] at hLR
      obtain ⟨⟨hLcard, hLindep⟩, ⟨⟨hRcard, hRindep⟩, hvR⟩⟩ := hLR
      have hdisj : Disjoint (leftCopy L) (rightCopy R) := by
        apply Finset.disjoint_left.mpr
        intro x hxL hxR
        simp only [leftCopy, rightCopy, Finset.mem_image] at hxL hxR
        obtain ⟨a, _, rfl⟩ := hxL; obtain ⟨b, _, h⟩ := hxR
        exact Sum.inl_ne_inr h.symm
      have hLRcard : (leftCopy L ∪ rightCopy R).card = r := by
        rw [Finset.card_union_of_disjoint hdisj]; simp [hLcard, hRcard]; omega
      refine ⟨leftCopy L ∪ rightCopy R, ?_, ?_⟩
      · simp only [Sk, Finset.mem_filter, mem_vertexStar_iff, mem_indepRSets_iff]
        refine ⟨⟨⟨hLRcard, ?_⟩, by simp [mem_rightCopy, hvR]⟩, ?_⟩
        · -- IsIndepSet (disjointUnionSelf G) (leftCopy L ∪ rightCopy R)
          intro x hxLR y hyLR
          simp only [Finset.mem_union, leftCopy, rightCopy, Finset.mem_image] at hxLR hyLR
          rcases hxLR with ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ | ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ <;>
          rcases hyLR with ⟨b, hb, rfl⟩ | ⟨b, hb, rfl⟩
          · exact hLindep a ha b hb
          · simp [disjointUnionSelf]
          · simp [disjointUnionSelf]
          · exact hRindep a ha b hb
        · -- (leftPreimage (leftCopy L ∪ rightCopy R)).card = k
          have : leftPreimage (leftCopy L ∪ rightCopy R) = L := by
            ext w; simp [leftPreimage_mem_iff]
          rw [this, hLcard]
      · simp only [Prod.mk.injEq]
        exact ⟨by ext w; simp [leftPreimage_mem_iff],
               by ext w; simp [rightPreimage_mem_iff]⟩
  -- Step C: The star decomposes as biUnion (Icc 0 (r-1)) Sk;
  -- separate k=0 from k≥1, apply hSk0 and hSkk.
  -- Every S in the star has leftPreimage size in Icc 0 (r-1) (since it contains inr v).
  have hmem_star : ∀ S ∈ vertexStar (disjointUnionSelf G) (Sum.inr v) r,
      (leftPreimage S).card ∈ Finset.Icc 0 (r - 1) := by
    intro S hS
    simp only [mem_vertexStar_iff, mem_indepRSets_iff, Finset.mem_Icc] at hS ⊢
    obtain ⟨⟨hcard, _⟩, hvS⟩ := hS
    refine ⟨Nat.zero_le _, ?_⟩
    have hRne : v ∈ rightPreimage S := (rightPreimage_mem_iff S v).mpr hvS
    have hRpos : 0 < (rightPreimage S).card := Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨v, hRne⟩
    have := card_eq_left_plus_right S; rw [hcard] at this; omega
  have hstar_eq : vertexStar (disjointUnionSelf G) (Sum.inr v) r =
      Finset.biUnion (Finset.Icc 0 (r - 1)) Sk := by
    ext S
    simp only [Finset.mem_biUnion, Sk, Finset.mem_filter]
    exact ⟨fun hS => ⟨(leftPreimage S).card, hmem_star S hS, hS, rfl⟩,
           fun ⟨_, _, hS, rfl⟩ => hS⟩
  have hdisj_Sk : ∀ i ∈ Finset.Icc 0 (r - 1), ∀ j ∈ Finset.Icc 0 (r - 1),
      i ≠ j → Disjoint (Sk i) (Sk j) := by
    intro i _ j _ hij
    apply Finset.disjoint_filter.mpr
    intro S _ hi hj; exact hij (hi.symm.trans hj)
  have hIcc_split : Finset.Icc 0 (r - 1) = {0} ∪ Finset.Icc 1 (r - 1) := by
    ext k; simp only [Finset.mem_Icc, Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_singleton]; omega
  have h01disj : Disjoint ({0} : Finset ℕ) (Finset.Icc 1 (r - 1)) := by
    simp
  rw [hstar_eq, Finset.card_biUnion hdisj_Sk, hIcc_split,
      Finset.sum_union h01disj, Finset.sum_singleton, hSk0]
  congr 1
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl hSkk

Proved by slicing the star by left-part size and using Finset.card_bij for the bijection. The decomposition lemma leftCopy_leftPreimage_union_rightCopy_rightPreimage and preimage membership simp lemmas are also fully proved here.
